result.topic_en: Contiguous relations of the hypergeometric series F(α,β,γ) and its derivative F', leading to the hypergeometric differential equation and its transformation under x → 1−x.
result.transcription:

[17] $F'(\alpha,\beta+1,\gamma+1) = \frac{\alpha\gamma}{(\alpha-\gamma)x}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) - \frac{\gamma(\gamma-\alpha x)}{\beta(\alpha-\gamma)x}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
[18] $F(\alpha-1,\beta,\gamma-1) = \frac{\gamma-1-\beta x}{\gamma-1}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{x-xx}{\gamma-1}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
[19] $F(\alpha,\beta-1,\gamma-1) = \frac{\gamma-1-\alpha x}{\gamma-1}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{x-xx}{\gamma-1}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
[20] $F'(\alpha-1,\beta,\gamma-1) = \frac{(\alpha-1)\beta}{\gamma-1}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{(\alpha-1)x}{\gamma-1}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
[21] $F'(\alpha,\beta-1,\gamma-1) = \frac{\alpha(\beta-1)}{\gamma-1}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{(\beta-1)x}{\gamma-1}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$

[26] $F(\alpha+1,\beta+1,\gamma+1) = \frac{\gamma}{\alpha\beta}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
[27] $F'(\alpha+1,\beta+1,\gamma+1) = \frac{\gamma}{x-xx}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) - \frac{\gamma(\gamma-(\alpha+\beta+1)x)}{\alpha\beta(x-xx)}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
[28] $F(\alpha-1,\beta-1,\gamma-1) =$
[29] $F'(\alpha-1,\beta-1,\gamma-1) = \frac{(\alpha-1)(\beta-1)}{\gamma-1}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
Das bisherige bekannt gemacht Comment. Recent. Soc. Gott. T. II.

Aus der Verbindung der Gleichungen 1 und 27 folgt nun leicht, wenn man die zweite derivirte Function durch $F''(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ bezeichnet
[30] $\alpha\beta F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) - (\gamma-(\alpha+\beta+1)x)F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) [-+-] - (x-xx)F''(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) = 0.$
Es sei P der Werth von $F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$, [-für-] und Q der Werth derselben Function, wenn man für $x$, $1-x$ setzt. Man hat dann
$\alpha\beta P - (\gamma-(\alpha+\beta+1)x)\frac{dP}{dx} [-+-] - (x-xx)\frac{d^2P}{dx^2} = 0$
$\alpha\beta Q - (\alpha+\beta+1-\gamma-(\alpha+\beta+1)x)\frac{dQ}{dx} [-+-] - (x-xx)\frac{d^2Q}{dx^2} = 0$ also, für den Fall, wo $2\gamma = \alpha+\beta+1$ ist, welcher eine besondre Aufmerksamkeit verdient
